new_statements.quote: Систематических сдвигов гласных, по-видимому, нет. Гласные артикулируются так же, как соответствующие им звуки в нганасанском или долганском языках; это является абсолютно нормальным, учитывая, что говорка для всех ее носителей остается неродным языком. Место ударения в большинстве случаев также сохраняется (поэтому в приводимых здесь примерах ударение обычно не отмечается); по крайней мере некоторые отличия объясняются диалектными различиями внутри русского языка. Интонационные контуры совпадают с нганасанскими во всех деталях.
new_statements.translation: There appear to be no systematic vowel shifts. Vowels are articulated like the corresponding sounds of Nganasan or Dolgan; this is entirely normal given that Govorka remains a non-native language for all its speakers. The place of stress is in most cases also preserved [i.e. as in Russian] (which is why stress is usually not marked in the examples cited here); at least some of the divergences are explained by dialect differences within Russian. Intonation contours coincide with those of Nganasan in every detail.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress in Govorka falls where it falls in the Russian source word (Russian free, lexically specified stress is retained) in most cases; the few deviations from standard Russian stress placement are attributed at least partly to Russian dialect variation (North Russian / Siberian colloquial input), not to a pidgin-internal stress rule. Phrase intonation, by contrast, is Nganasan.
new_statements.exceptions: 'In most cases' — some words deviate from standard Russian stress; Helimski attributes at least some of these to Russian-internal dialect differences; no list given. Examples are written in Russian orthography without stress marks except where relevant (e.g. postposition место pronounced мéста).
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is about word stress in lexical items relative to the Russian etyma (word domain); intonation contours (phrase level) are separately said to be Nganasan. Author's transcription policy: Russian orthography, only essential phonetic differences noted.
new_statements.identity_note: Helimski's description is of Govorka as spoken by elderly Nganasan speakers in Ust'-Avam and Volochanka (fieldwork from 1986; principal consultants Tubyaku Kosterkin, Numumu Turdagin, Numare Yarotsky, Karare Kokore), i.e. the same variety Glottolog lists as taim1252 Taimyr Pidgin Russian; he notes Dolgan, Enets and Nenets speakers confirmed the same forms. The stress statement is relative to the lexifier: Russian (Siberian colloquial, with North Russian dialect traits) word stress is retained.
